rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or Evaluator feedback yet, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract's physics. Geometry: five line sensors spread across the centre line (x = -0.04 to +0.04 m, step 0.02 m) and 0.04 m ahead of the axle, so the robot sees the line before it reaches the wheels. The 12 mm footprint is wide enough to keep readings non-zero on curves while staying narrow enough to resolve the 25 mm tape edge. Sensor weights are antisymmetric (-2, -1, 0, +1, +2), so a positive signal (tape on the left) steers left, which matches the contract's sign convention. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give a moderate turn rate and a speed ceiling that should allow completing a 4 to 5 m course in under 3 s. Mass 0.8 kg keeps yaw inertia low, so turns respond quickly. Controller: base_speed 1.8 (near full PWM) to meet the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed. kp 4.0 gives a clear steering response without saturating the 350-count differential. kd 0.2 damps the overshoot a proportional-only loop would show on sharp bends. ki 0.2 is small, to remove steady bias from the fixed motor mismatch without windup. line_loss last_direction recovers toward the side the line was last seen. Expected result: completion on the development tracks with a few line-loss events at the sharpest bend. Hypotheses to test: (1) kp around 4 is near the oscillation threshold at speed 1.8, so steering_oscillation will show whether kd must rise; (2) the 0.04 m sensor lead is enough, which max_error will confirm; (3) base_speed 1.8 may be too fast for the sharpest curve, which shows as max_error growth and line_loss_events on the slalom track. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation, so the next revision can tune speed against stability.
